Alex.confusing: How the Turkey and Eagle eggs worked. Several players, me included, argued over who gains an egg from a visit, and the Eagle's "eggs for every visitor" wording was ambiguous.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when I used the Owl result to point out the Casey and Drew Turkey contradiction. Winning round 3 as the Mouser and banking 13 points was also satisfying.
Alex.change: Make the Turkey and Eagle wording clearer, and give the winners a smaller edge so one early lead doesn't decide the whole game.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw my D10 and H7 at Blair on a weak consensus. They were discarded when we lost, and that cost me my best cards. I'd have thrown lower cards and kept the high ones.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count was easy to misread: Finley and I both took it as counting visitors to me, when it counts visitors to my target. Confused dawn reports, like Finley's Kookaburra, also made the table's egg logic harder to trust.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was a tangle: Casey, Drew and Ellis all made Turkey claims that kept contradicting the egg rule, and the table turned on itself while I was secretly the Floofer.
Blair.change: Publish each player's visit targets and egg changes in a single summary at each dawn, so claims like the Turkey and Eagle counts can be checked without the table having to reconstruct them from memory.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw low cards at Ellis, a Farm Hawk, and let the Meowfia Sphinx Drew survive; I should have checked who was silent and thrown at Drew, since Drew dodged the role question for two beats.

Casey.confusing: Whether the Turkey's egg goes to the visitor or the Turkey. Several players, including me, muddled it mid-argument, and that cost me credibility in round 2.
Casey.fun: Winking Alex as the Mouser in round 2 and watching the table turn on Drew. Banking 20 points that round also put me in second.
Casey.change: Give the Mouser a clearer way to pick targets and make Turkey-style interactions easier to check. I'd also do something about the runaway leader, because Ellis's 29 after round 1 was close to decisive.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I claimed Hawk and said I'd visited Drew, who had not yet claimed Turkey. That contradicted his Turkey claim and got me suspected. I should have claimed a role that no other claim could contradict, or visited a player more likely to stay quiet. In round 3 I could also have thrown fewer cards and kept more as a floor, since Ellis was already far ahead.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey rule and the Eagle/Owl egg counts were hard to pin down, and I got the Turkey direction wrong in round 2, which muddied the table. Confused dawn reports also made other players' egg counts unreliable.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: as Sphinx I learned Finley was the Kookaburra, then had to bluff a Farm Owl claim while the table argued over Casey and Ellis.
Drew.change: I'd make the Turkey and Eagle egg rules clearer in the dawn reports, and state whether a visit counts for the target or the visitor, so players stop miscounting.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I invented a false Owl claim and threw a card at Ellis, when staying quiet and using my Sphinx knowledge of Finley more carefully would have been less exposed. I'd keep my claims minimal next time.

Ellis.confusing: How the Turkey and Hawk eggs interact: a Hawk visiting a Turkey gets an egg from the Turkey too. That made my Hawk egg impossible to tell apart from a Meowfia hit, and the table argued about it for a long time.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when I was Meowfia. I bluffed as Falcon, and the whole table piled onto Blair, who was Farm. That banked 27 points in one throw.
Ellis.change: Let Hawk and Turkey eggs be told apart. A Hawk could learn why it gained an egg, or the Turkey's egg could be flagged on the dawn report. As it is, a truthful Hawk can't prove anything.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I loudly claimed Hawk and said Casey was Meowfia. Casey was a Turkey, so the egg was only from her ability. I should have kept my role quiet or claimed something vaguer, because I became the eggsecution target and lost the round.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey rule and the Eagle count were hard to pin down: the Turkey's egg went to visitors, and players argued about it for several beats. My own confused dawn report also made my Kookaburra read unreliable.
Finley.fun: Watching the table converge on Blair in round 1 and then cross-examine the Turkey and Eagle stories in round 2 was engaging. Casey's late flip to Drew was a good moment.
Finley.change: Have the Storyteller state each visit and egg result more explicitly, so claims like the Turkey and Eagle counts can be checked without long arguments.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I switched my throw to Drew, who was Farm, when Casey was the Mouser whose Hawk-to-Turkey story didn't add up. I would keep pressing Casey and avoid throwing on a shifting claim.
